It is one of Buenos Aires’ most emblematic and charming neighborhoods. Located in the heart of the city, Monserrat is home to one of its most important squares: Plaza de Mayo. Weaving through the neighborhood is the city’s busiest and most iconic avenue, giving Monserrat a central location that not only connects with the pulse of Buenos Aires, but also makes it easy to access public transportation to explore other neighborhoods. Monserrat, a neighborhood with history Monserrat presents a parade of buildings that breathe the essence of history—from the Metropolitan Cathedral to the majestic Teatro Colón—enhancing the experience of those who wander its streets. As one of the city’s oldest areas, Monserrat owes its name to the creation of the Brotherhood of Our Lady of Montserrat, where the church of the devotees of the Virgin Mary—venerated in Catalonia, Spain—was founded. Its cobblestone streets are pathways through key events in Argentine independence, while its colonial buildings and imposing squares—such as the Metropolitan Cathedral on Plaza de Mayo—stand as silent witnesses to the greatness and struggle of a nation in the making. 5 things you can’t miss in Monserrat 1. Historic Tour of Plaza de Mayo: Don’t miss a visit to historic Plaza de Mayo, where the Casa Rosada, the Cabildo, and the Metropolitan Cathedral will transport you to Argentina’s foundational moments. 2. Stroll Along the Cobblestone Streets: Monserrat is perfect for exploring on foot. Its stone-paved streets will lead you to small antique shops, used-book stores, and charming hidden corners. 3. Porteño Gastronomy: Be sure to try the delicious local cuisine. From traditional parrillas serving succulent Argentine asados to fine-dining restaurants that fuse flavors from around the world, Monserrat has options for every palate. 4. City Museum: Immerse yourself in Buenos Aires’ history through the exhibits and collections at the City Museum, which take you from colonial origins to the present day. 5. Enjoy Tango: Buenos Aires is the cradle of tango, and in Monserrat you’ll find milongas and live tango shows where you can feel the passion of this iconic dance.
